HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident on 04/23/2023, driver, sideswiped on the driver's side. Initial orthopaedic evaluation of the left
shoulder. Right-hand dominant. Financial advisor at Northwestern Mutual, paid on commission; out of work since the
accident.
COMPLAINTS AND EXAMINATION
Left shoulder pain with reaching, dressing and overhead activity. Active forward elevation 110 degrees and abduction 90
degrees, limited by pain. Distal hand function and sensation grossly intact.
ASSESSMENT
Persistent left shoulder symptoms following the reported motor vehicle accident. Shoulder MRI findings are not yet available
at this visit.
PLAN
Further left shoulder evaluation and MRI review when available. Activity modification and follow-up. No operative date is
established in this initial visit.

Motor vehicle accident on 04/23/2023, driver, sideswiped on the driver's side. Left shoulder symptoms persist. Pre-operative
consultation for left shoulder arthroscopy.
IMAGING AND EXAMINATION
The 05/24/2023 left shoulder MRI describes the posterior inferior labral tear, low-grade posterior infraspinatus interstitial
tear, inferior glenohumeral ligament thickening and posterior inferior glenoid hypoplasia. Active shoulder motion remains
painful.
OPERATIVE PLANNING
Left shoulder examination under anesthesia and arthroscopy planned for 07/26/2023 with Dr. David Capiola at New Horizon
Surgical Center, LLC. Procedure options reviewed in relation to the documented shoulder findings.
PLAN
Proceed with the planned left shoulder procedure and postoperative rehabilitation. This note addresses the left shoulder; it
does not schedule a right shoulder procedure.

HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident on 04/23/2023, driver, sideswiped on the driver's side.
PROCEDURE AND SITE
Left shoulder examination under anesthesia and arthroscopy. Surgeon: David Capiola, M.D. Site: New Horizon Surgical
Center, LLC, 680 Broadway, Suite 201, Paterson, NJ 07514. This is the surgeon copy maintained in the McCulloch chart.
PROCEDURES PERFORMED
Posterior labral repair with a 2.99 mm BioComposite PushLock anchor and a cinch stitch; complete synovectomy; lysis of
adhesions; subacromial decompression; debridement of the biceps tendon, partial rotator cuff tear and cartilage defect.
POST-OPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS
Significant posterior labral tear, synovitis, adhesions, impingement, biceps tendon partial tear, partial rotator cuff tear,
cartilage defect.
